propositions: Extraction from free-text JSON is heuristic and vulnerable to trailing schema-valid decoys winning over the intended payload, especially when models fence-wrap quoted content.

An explicit line-anchored sentinel marker channel (<<<REBAR_OUTPUT>>>/<<<END>>>) must wrap the single final JSON object, with markers recognized only when alone on their own line, to make payload location a deterministic contract rather than an inference.

The extraction parser must honor markers with last-block-wins semantics (reverse-order iteration over complete blocks), fall back to schema-filtered full-reply selection when no complete blocks exist, and fail-closed (raise validation error) when markers are present but all blocks are invalid.

Marker pairing follows a left-to-right, non-nested rule: each <<<REBAR_OUTPUT>>> pairs with the next <<<END>>>, and incomplete/interleaved markers (open without close, or repeated opens before a single close) are disambiguated deterministically by this rule.
The bounded-retry prompt must name the same markers as the first attempt, so the fail-closed retry channel (layer 4) is consistent and prevents a second-attempt decoy from winning.

The single-sourced SENTINEL_DIRECTIVE constant must be used by schema_directive(), the marker extractor, the retry tail, and the measurement harness, with no drift between what the model is instructed to emit and what the parser looks for.
